title: Hometown Region
text: “Did something happen?”
“Well… it’s honestly the kind of situation I’m struggling to explain, but for that guy’s sake, I’d really appreciate it if you could come. More than anything, please stop the one called Rafumi!”

“Umm, so like—Dark Sacred Hero Mark Two is trying to teach the succession method to the second-generation Jet-Black Love Transmitter, but he’s refusing, so now she’s trying to force him into being a sacrifice—?”

Father and Ren exchanged a glance, and since there was nothing else for it, they ended up going along, I say. Just what had Rafumi gone and done? Since there seemed to be a chance to grab some leverage out of this, Motoyasu decided to tag along too. As for whatever Kuro-chan was going on about, Motoyasu had absolutely no idea what any of it meant.
“Well then, let us summon Filolial-sama! Yuki-chan!”
“Yes, ma’am!”
Motoyasu wanted to call for Filo-tan, but she’d gone off to play with Big Sister and the others, so she wasn’t around.
“Don’t you dare call Luna!”
Ren made absolutely sure to hammer that point home. Just how badly did Ren dislike Luna-chan, anyway?
“I don’t really get it, but let’s just go already.”

And so, guided by Ren’s companions, we headed off toward the scene, indeed. From what Motoyasu overheard along the way, it seemed the whole thing started when they ran into bandits during an escort job they’d taken on from the guild.
“Just shut up and go home already.”
“Not even if I die! I swore I’d never set foot in that house again!”
“I get how you feel, given that old man of yours, but you can’t just go turning to banditry!”

So, when they arrived, there was Rafumi, apparently in the middle of barking orders at a captured bandit. Nearby, the leader of Ren’s companions stood with furrowed brows, gazing at the bandit with obvious concern. The rest of the bandits, meanwhile, lay tied up and rolling on the ground, looking thoroughly baffled by the whole affair.
“So, what exactly is going on here?”
“Ah, Ren-sama, Shield Hero-sama!”
“Welt, sounds like you’re the one who called us out here—so what happened?”

Was this inult-Ren really going to fix anything just by showing up? Motoyasu had his doubts, indeed. Ren looked back and forth between the bandit, who kept refusing something, and Rafumi, who was radiating murderous intent like some kind of interrogator.
“No… well, we were in the middle of an escort job when we ran into bandits. We fought them off and took them prisoner, which was fine and all, but, well, one of them turned out to be someone I know.”
“And you want us to let him off the hook?”
Ren crossed his arms and sighed, as if to say that acquaintance or not, a criminal was a criminal and ought to be turned in without delay.

“Er… it’s not that there’s none of that in it. Well, instead of letting him go, if he properly turned his heart back toward his dream, I thought maybe I could vouch for him. More like—we left the village together, so I guess I wanted to root for him.”
Apparently, the leader of Ren’s companions and this bandit were old acquaintances from the same hometown.
“Like I said before—why’d you sink so low as to become a bandit? You used to have a dream of making it as an adventurer, didn’t you…?”
“Shut up! I just… I just…!”

The bandit, glaring back under Rafumi’s watchful eye, spat the words bitterly at the leader of Ren’s companions. Bandit on one side, hero’s companion on the other—he probably meant to point out just how far apart their standings had drifted.
“I couldn’t claw my way up the way you did! Don’t you go assuming things just work out fine for everyone!”
Back in the very first world, this fellow had apparently made quite a name for himself as Father’s pet righteous thief. Sounds like things worked out pretty well, in Motoyasu’s humble opinion.
“So, why exactly is he… you know, all tangled up with Rafumi-chan?”

“Honestly, I’m not too sure myself. Right when I was thinking I’d hand him over to the vigilante corps if he showed no remorse, he’d apparently been disguised as Ren-sama, but then he turned back into his real form and started insisting, over and over, that he was heading home to his parents’ place… and, well, things sort of got out of hand.”
“Rafumi-chan, what’s wrong?”
Father asked Rafumi. She turned, fixed the bandit with a glare, and finally spoke.
“The Shield Hero, is it. Perfect timing—I intend to drag this one back to his parents’ house.”
“No way! I’d rather die than go back to a place like that! I won’t go back to that house even if you kill me!”
“Hmhmhm, no matter what happens, I won’t kill you… much like how the Spear Hero once executed Takt, there’s something I need you to do first, you see.”
“W-wait, did this bandit step on the exact same landmine that once sent Motoyasu-kun into a bottomless rage?”
Father eyed the bandit with a look of visible retreat.

“Are you people even higher up than this guy!? If it means not getting sent home, I don’t care if it’s the vigilante corps or the whole kingdom—take me anywhere! I’ll take whatever punishment you throw at me!”
The bandit cried out for salvation. Hm… he did seem to be an old acquaintance of Ren’s companion leader, but what in the world was actually going on here?
“Welt, what exactly is the deal with this guy’s—well, your—hometown?”
“Er… his family runs a perfectly ordinary chocolate farm.”
“I feel like the words ‘chocolate farm’ alone put this pretty far from ‘ordinary.’”
“Exactly! What do you mean, a chocolate farm!? Shouldn’t it be cacao!?”
Father said this rather delicately, while Ren pointed it out with considerably more force.
“Huh? Is a chocolate farm really that strange?”
The leader of Ren’s companions asked, looking around at everyone. Everyone else nodded in agreement.
“I wouldn’t call it strange exactly, but it’s definitely a rare, specialized line of farming. At the very least, it’s nowhere near common.”
“I’ve heard it’s difficult to cultivate.”
The mages among Ren’s companions nodded along in agreement.
“I see. So it’s rare, but it does exist as an actual trade. Guess that’s just how things go in another world, huh? I get cacao, but farming chocolate itself…”

Indeed, that much was true. Farms that raised trees bearing actual chocolate fruit were unique to this world, and moreover, they were specialty operations tied to the Valentine’s season. Motoyasu recalled hearing that Father apparently went shopping for some whenever the season rolled around. Come to think of it, this was also the native habitat of the very chocolate monster that had originally given rise to Rafumi. Motoyasu remembered one showing up in the village once—the uproar back then had been considerable, indeed. In the end, one had even appeared in Zeltoble and caused no small amount of damage. In the middle of all that chaos, Rival had used a chocolate monster’s body to appear in the very first world, and Motoyasu had struck it down once, I say.
“Speaking of the event region—wouldn’t Ren know about it? It’s the site of the Valentine’s event.”
“Ah… that event. So Welt, you’re from that region?”
“Wow, that alone tells you where he’s from? I have no clue what you two are even talking about.”

“Long ago, a hero created a tree that bears chocolate fruit, and the monsters born nearby come from that chocolate. And as it happens, I myself also serve as a spirit born of that very Valentine’s event.”
Rafumi was the assassin Ren had created after taking his solitary tendencies a little too far—the fruit of years of dedicated research, apparently.
“So, Rafumi-chan. This guy really doesn’t want to go home, huh…?”

“Ah, this one’s father is a truly foolish old man who does nothing but fool around with chocolate, Valentine’s Day included. From where I stand, much like how the Spear Hero dealt with Takt, this is someone who absolutely must be made to answer for what he’s done. And this one here, who let him run wild unchecked, shares equally in that guilt—so I can’t rest easy without giving him a proper dose of harassment.”
“Wow… that sounds rough.”
“Take a good long look at this face and remember it well. Now that I’ve caught you, perfect timing—off to your house we go, I say.”
“That’s exactly why I don’t want to! I don’t want anything to do with that man ever again!”

So that was just how much he hated it. Motoyasu recalled hearing this was in fact his real father, though—well, even back in his own world, plenty of pigs got tangled up with rotten relatives, so this sort of thing was probably nothing too unusual. Sometimes it was just a misunderstanding that could be patched up through reconciliation, but when it came to truly hopeless, garbage relatives, well—that was really a case-by-case matter, indeed.
